title: Project Proposal
text:
Research Questions
1. In which majors is the GPA most affected by heavier AI Usage?
2. How can AI be used for the best GPA score?
The audience for this analysis are students which want to understand how much AI is good and normal to use in their field for a better grade. The overall message is more important then the details for this scenario, so simple visualizations like graphs without clutter should work best.

title: Project Proposal
text:
Analysis Plan

The most important variable I am going to use is the GPA as the goal is to measure the student performance affected by AI.
For question 1 I also need the weekly generative AI study hours and the traditional study hours to measure how heavy the student’s AI usage is in procents. Other variables like tool diversity might also be interesting for this even though less important.
For question 2 the variables paid subscriptions and tool diversity are important, but also the primary use case.
The uncertainties are less of a incomplete or flawed dataset, but which variables are fair to be weighed against another to give the best persepctive for the questions.

title: Project Proposal
text:
The source of the data is:
https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/laveshjadon/ai-impact-on-students?select=ai_student_impact_dataset+%281%29.csv
The data is licenced under CC0 1.0 Universal:
(https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)
Content:
The dataset “Impact of Ai on Students” is about the generative AI usage of students and its effects on them. There are 50000 rows representing 50000 observed students. Also 16 observed features are listed in its 16 columns. They capture various key information of the students (e.g. their major, study year & GPA score), but also how they use generative AI (e.g. which tools they use, which usecase they have & their prompting skills).
Where does the data come from?
The data is synthetically generated as stated in the provenance tab of the source.
However I reason that the data is sensibly created and is suitable for further research for the following reasons:
- good documentation (namely the creation process)
- vastly exposed to public in form of downloads, discussions or notebooks
- the creator has a comprehensive track record on kaggle
